topics.title: Visual Studio IDE & Its Windows

According to the chapter summary, which extension is used for an SQL database file?

topics.title: CodeBehind & Inline Code
topics.description: CodeBehind vs inline code, file naming, the @Page directive and the Page_Init / Page_Load events.

questions.prompt: What is CodeBehind?

options.text: Code written inside the HTML in the same file
ASP.NET page code written in a separate class file from the markup

questions.explanation: It separates presentation (HTML, CSS) from execution code (C#, VB.NET).

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of CodeBehind? (select all that apply)

options.text: Separates logic and presentation, making maintenance easier
Works with server controls, which can interact with the code behind the page

questions.prompt: The Web Form is mypage.aspx and the language is C#. What is the CodeBehind file's name?
questions.explanation: The CodeBehind file name matches the Web Form, plus .cs for C# (or .vb for VB.NET).

questions.prompt: Which extension does a VB.NET CodeBehind file use?
What is INLINE code?

options.text: Server-side code written directly inside the .aspx page, alongside the HTML, in a <script> block

questions.prompt: Which model stores markup and server-side code in SEPARATE files (Default.aspx + Default.aspx.cs)?
A page has only Default.aspx, with the C# code inside it. Which model is that?
When are scripting blocks (<% %>) suitable?

options.text: For simple scripts — CodeBehind is better for larger logic

questions.prompt: What does the @Page directive do?

options.text: Sets default properties for the whole page, such as the default language

questions.prompt: In the @Page directive, what does the CodeBehind property identify?

options.text: The path and filename of the CodeBehind file

questions.prompt: In the @Page directive, what does the Inherits property indicate?

options.text: That the code behind the page inherits the page class (which holds the page's compiled code)

questions.prompt: Which page event comes first and initialises the page control hierarchy (according to your notes)?
questions.explanation: Page_Init, then Page_Load. (Strictly, ASP.NET also has a Page_PreInit event before Page_Init, but your notes list Page_Init as the first.)

questions.prompt: Which page event loads server controls into memory and runs EVERY time the page executes?
Which object-oriented parts can a CodeBehind file contain? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The page class uses inheritance, e.g. `public partial class Default : System.Web.UI.Page`.

questions.prompt: How do you open the CodeBehind file in Visual Studio?

options.text: In Solution Explorer, expand the Web Form and double-click the .aspx.cs file

questions.explanation: It opens in the Document Window.

questions.prompt: After adding code to the CodeBehind file, which keys run the app (without debugging)?
questions.explanation: Save first, then Ctrl + F5 and check the browser output.

topics.title: Event Handlers
topics.description: Events, event-driven ASP.NET, event-handler structure, sender and e, and adding a button event in Design view.

questions.prompt: What is an event?

options.text: An action or occurrence, such as a mouse click, key press or system notification

questions.prompt: Which of these are events? (select all that apply)
ASP.NET Web Forms applications are entirely event-driven.
In Web Forms, where is the event-handling code added?
What is the return type of an ASP.NET event handler?
questions.explanation: The pattern is `void EventName(object sender, EventArgs e)`. Your notes write it as private; Visual Studio usually generates `protected void Button1_Click(...)` for Web Forms — both return void.

questions.prompt: In `EventName(object sender, EventArgs e)`, what is sender?

options.text: The object that raised the event

questions.prompt: In the same signature, what is e?

options.text: The object that raised the event

questions.prompt: The user types Ali into txtName and clicks the button. What text does lblResult show?
questions.explanation: The handler joins "Hello, " with the TextBox's text.

questions.prompt: How do you open the Web Form Designer?

options.text: Right-click the .aspx file and choose “View Designer”

questions.explanation: The Web Form opens in Design view.

questions.prompt: In Design view, what happens when you double-click a Button?

options.text: A new event-handler method is created in the CodeBehind file

questions.prompt: What is the correct order when testing a button event?

options.text: Click the button → run the app → type text → result
Run the app → type into the TextBox → click the button → the handler runs → the result is displayed
Type text → result → run the app → click

topics.title: Compilation & Runtime Errors
topics.description: Build-time vs run-time failures, the execution pipeline, types of compilation errors and runtime exceptions.

questions.prompt: A COMPILATION error happens at which stage?

options.text: Build time — detected by the C# compiler
Run time — detected by the .NET runtime

questions.prompt: A RUNTIME error happens at which stage?

options.text: While a successfully built program is executing

questions.prompt: Why can't a program with a compilation error run?

options.text: The compiler can't translate the source code into IL, so the build fails

questions.prompt: In .NET, how are runtime errors represented?
What is the correct C# execution pipeline?
questions.explanation: Compilation errors are caught at the compiler stage; runtime errors at the runtime stage.

questions.prompt: What type of compilation error is this?
What type of compilation error is this?
questions.explanation: A string can't be assigned to an int.

questions.prompt: What type of compilation error is this?
questions.explanation: Same name twice in the same scope.

questions.prompt: What type of compilation error is `UnknownType obj = new();`?
questions.explanation: The compiler can't find the type.

questions.prompt: Accessing a private field from another class causes which error?
In this program, which problem does the developer see FIRST?

options.text: The compilation error — `total` was never declared (CS0103)

questions.explanation: A program must build before it can run, so the runtime error only appears after the compilation error is fixed.

questions.prompt: Once `total` is fixed, what happens when the program runs?
questions.explanation: number2 is 0, so integer division by zero throws.

questions.prompt: Which compiler error code does your notes give for the undeclared variable `total`?
questions.explanation: CS0103: The name 'total' does not exist in the current context.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: Accessing a member through a null reference.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: The valid indexes are 0, 1 and 2.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: "ABC" isn't a valid number format.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: The file doesn't exist.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: A string object can't be cast to int at runtime.

questions.prompt: Which runtime exception does this code throw?
questions.explanation: Integer division by zero.

questions.prompt: Which are common causes of RUNTIME errors? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Missing semicolons and undeclared variables are compilation errors.

questions.prompt: How do you fix a RUNTIME error? (select all that apply)
How do you fix a COMPILATION error?
